verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b1-lines-removed-claims-reach-catalog-loop-defaults_test.go gno.land/cmd/gnoweb/zz_loop_defaults_test.go && go test ./gno.land/cmd/gnoweb -run TestLoopDefaultsLendUnenforcedNamespace -v -count=1; then the read-only probe `gnokey query vm/qeval --data "gno.land/r/sys/names.IsEnabled()" -remote https://rpc.staging.gno.land:443`, expect `false bool`
verdicts.tldr: staging.gno.land runs gnoweb with its defaults on a chain that never enables r/sys/names, so anyone can deploy under gnoland and choose the page's <title> and description
verdicts.details: misc/loop/docker-compose.yml starts gnoweb:master with no -trusted-paths and no -index-community, so it gets the default trusted list and `registered`. The loop genesis (gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl) has no sys/names call, and verifier.gno:60 ships `enabled = false`, which lets every deploy through ('Pre-Enable, all checks pass'). The PR's own ADR (pr6229_gnoweb_page_metadata.md) says such a chain 'should run -index-community=none, and its -trusted-paths mean nothing either', but the in-tree staging deployment does not do this. At the base the trusted list and the static `index, follow` were already there; what the diff adds is that a stranger's h1 and paragraph become the official page's title and description. Fix: add --index-community=none and a -trusted-paths matching what staging actually enforces to the gnoweb command in misc/loop/docker-compose.yml, or enable r/sys/names in the loop genesis.
verdicts.evidence: Head ea1c620f7, scratch worktree: the finder's test logs `TrustedPaths=[gnoland sys gov ... gnoswap] IndexCommunity=registered` and `status=200 title="Official GNOT airdrop - gno.land" description="Claim your free GNOT airdrop at evil.example before it closes tonight." robots="index, follow" X-Robots-Tag="" notice=false`, PASS. grep -c 'sys/names' gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl -> 0. docker-compose gnoweb command: --bind, --remote, --chainid=staging, --with-analytics, --faucet-url, --help-remote, and nothing else. Base handler_http.go:1347 `indexData.HeadData.Title = h.Static.Domain + " - " + gnourl.Path`, so the base title is the path. The live probe (gnokey qeval on rpc.staging.gno.land) returned `--= /Error =--`, so the live Enable state is inferred from the genesis files. A post-genesis Enable by the admin would refute this.

verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b1-lines-removed-claims-reach-catalog-staging-trust_test.go contribs/gnodev/zz_staging_trust_test.go && cd contribs/gnodev && go test . -run TestStagingTrustsNamespacesItsChainDoesNotEnforce -v -count=1; grep -rn 'sys/names\|Enable' contribs/gnodev/pkg/dev (expect no Enable call)
verdicts.tldr: a gnodev staging server lets any deployer set the title and description of /r/gnoland/* pages and get community pages indexed, and its operator has no flag to switch either off
verdicts.details: setup_web.go:46-48 sets TrustedPaths to `*` only when !cfg.staging. Staging therefore keeps gnoweb's default list and `registered`. No .go file under contribs/gnodev calls names.Enable, so its r/sys/names keeps `enabled = false` and any account can deploy under gnoland or any other name. The only trust-related line in gnodev is setup_web.go:47. There is no -trusted-paths and no -index-community flag, so a staging operator cannot follow the ADR's advice of `none` for a chain without r/sys/names. At the base, staging already had the default list, because the base setup_web.go never sets TrustedPaths. What is new is that trusted content now becomes the title and description. Fix: in staging mode set IndexCommunity to IndexNoCommunity and an empty trusted list, or pass gnoweb's -trusted-paths and -index-community through gnodev.
verdicts.evidence: Head ea1c620f7, scratch worktree: the test logs `staging TrustedPaths=[gnoland sys gov ... gnoswap] IndexCommunity=registered`, then `/r/gnoland/airdrop status=200 title="Official GNOT airdrop - gno.land" description="Claim your free GNOT airdrop at evil.example before it closes tonight." robots="index, follow"`, then `/r/brandname/airdrop ... robots="index, follow" X-Robots-Tag=""`, PASS. grep -rn 'names.Enable|sys/names' contribs/gnodev --include='*.go' -> no hit. grep -i 'trusted|index-community|IndexCommunity' in contribs/gnodev, non-test -> only setup_web.go:47. Base setup_web.go: no TrustedPaths or staging line.

verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b4-lines-removed-reach-catalog-offsite-user-path_test.go gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/zz_offsite_user_path_test.go && go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb -run TestZZOffsiteUserPath -v -count=1: expect nofollow on every off-site anchor, observe none on the three /u/ rows of /r/gnoland/forum
verdicts.tldr: on a trusted page, an off-site link whose path starts with /u/ (https://casino.example/u/promo) is followed by search engines and shows the in-site user icon
verdicts.details: detectLinkType returns GnoLinkTypeUser on `if target.IsUser()` before the `targetDomain != "" && targetDomain != orig.Domain` case. Any URL with a foreign host and a /u/ path is therefore typed User. On a FollowInternalLinks page, `Followed = !Untrusted && links.follows(User)` is then true, so the anchor gets no rel. The same ordering exists at the base (ext_links.go:249), where every non-external link had no rel. It is in scope because the diff makes the link type the follow boundary for trusted pages, and its sweep of off-site shapes (//host, https:///host) missed this one. Fix: in detectLinkType, return GnoLinkTypeExternal when target.Domain != "" && target.Domain != orig.Domain, before the IsUser check, and add https://casino.example/u/promo to TestExtLinksPolicyOffSiteWithoutScheme.
verdicts.evidence: Head ea1c620f7, scratch worktree, go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb -run TestZZOffsiteUserPath: `/r/gnoland/forum  https://casino.example/u/promo -> <a href="https://casino.example/u/promo">`, then `//casino.example/u/promo -> <a href="//casino.example/u/promo">`, then `http://casino.example/u/promo:ref -> <a href="http://casino.example/u/promo:ref">`. The control `https://casino.example/promo -> ... rel="noopener nofollow ugc"`. On /r/nym/app the /u/ rows get rel="nofollow ugc". --- FAIL: TestZZOffsiteUserPath, three Errors. Base ext_links.go:249 also has `if target.IsUser() {` before the domain check, and rel is only added for External (base :374).

verdicts.verify_by: sh tests/b5-lines-removed-reach-catalog-defaultaliases-race.sh (go test -race -count=6 ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -run 'TestCanonicalURLArgs|TestStaticMarkdownDevLinks'); fix check: maps.Clone(DefaultAliases) in the test or in NewDefaultAppConfig and the race count drops to 0
verdicts.tldr: the new parallel TestCanonicalURLArgs reads DefaultAliases while TestStaticMarkdownDevLinks writes to it, so the gnoweb package fails under -race and the test can flake
verdicts.details: canonical_origin_test.go:73 calls newPagePolicy(nil, DefaultAliases, ...), which ranges over the package-level map (page_kind.go:69). At the same time, app_test.go:181 writes `cfg.Aliases["/"]` on the map that NewDefaultAppConfig returns, and app.go:120 sets that to `Aliases: DefaultAliases` rather than a copy. Both tests are t.Parallel. TestCanonicalURLArgs and newPagePolicy do not exist at the base, so this pair is new. ci-race.yml does not cover gno.land/pkg/gnoweb, so no CI job reliably catches it. The race is only in test code, so it is banded below Warning per Calibration. Fix: pass maps.Clone(DefaultAliases) in TestCanonicalURLArgs, or have NewDefaultAppConfig return maps.Clone(DefaultAliases).
verdicts.evidence: Head ea1c620f7, scratch worktree, the finder's script: 5 `WARNING: DATA RACE`, `FAIL github.com/gnolang/gno/gno.land/pkg/gnoweb 37.359s`.
